natural_body: Deep discounts spike signups +31% but risk renewal. Use tactically with guardrails.

first.rationale:
The two degraded metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the same funnel stage, and the only direction that attacks both at their source rather than papering over them is onboarding simplification. Promotional pricing is the tempting answer given the competitor's entry pricing, but memory_73 is explicit that the +31% signup spike comes with renewal risk, and the objective here is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, not signup volume; buying price-sensitive SMB accounts against a competitor who can undercut further is a losing trade for this slot. Referral incentives (memory_57) work on established customers and do nothing for a broken top-of-funnel; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a real strength but addresses a segment that is not the one deteriorating.

I am spending both verification pulls on memory_86 and memory_31 because they are the load-bearing evidence for my chosen action and, critically, I cannot tell from the consolidated summaries whether they are two independent results or one experiment that got summarized twice at day 12 and day 52. If they trace to a single source record, my apparent convergent support collapses to one data point and I should downgrade to a small_guarded_test. I also want to see from the original records whether the reported lift was measured at first-week activation only or persisted to retention/conversion, since 'durable lift in first-week activation' is a claim about an early proxy metric, not about revenue.

Downstream risk flagged: memory_31's mechanism was cutting required fields at signup. Those fields plausibly feed lead qualification and routing, which is exactly what makes the demo-request path in memory_44 outperform on pipeline quality. Optimizing self-serve activation by stripping signup data could quietly degrade enterprise pipeline quality — a cost that shows up a quarter later and would not appear in the activation metric this experiment is scored on. I will instrument for lead-quality and demo-request-path effects, not just completion and activation.

Uncertainty preserved: all six memories are consolidated summaries of archived sources, all predate the competitor's price move, and none of them were measured in the current competitive environment. Prior lifts may not replicate against a changed alternative. I am treating the inherited record as a strong prior, not as settled fact, and the verification pulls are meant to test whether that prior is as well-supported as its phrasing suggests.
